# HerbAlly

> HerbAlly is a free, bilingual (English / French) evidence-graded clinical reference for medicinal herbs, herb–drug interactions, and pre-operative/clinical botanical safety. Covers 3,124 published herb profiles, 834 regulatory and classical monographs across 486 herbs (Health Canada, NIH LiverTox, EMA HMPC, NIH NCCIH, and pre-1930 dispensatories), 394 cited herb–drug interactions across 108 medications/classes, a Health Canada NPN/DIN-HM Decoder, a Multi-Herb Stack Checker, a Pre-Surgery Herb Washout Planner, and an adult dosage calculator. Editorially reviewed by Yasser Bheekun, MLT (OPTMQ · CSMLS). Free and open — no paywalls; advertising launch gate is currently off.

## Key resources

- Herb database (3,124 profiles): https://herbally.app/herbs
- Herb–drug interaction checker & Multi-Herb Stack Checker: https://herbally.app/herb-drug-interactions
- Reverse-lookup Medication Directory (108 drugs & classes A–Z): https://herbally.app/medications
- Curated herb–drug pair pages: https://herbally.app/interactions/[herb]/[drug] (e.g. https://herbally.app/interactions/st-johns-wort/fluoxetine)
- Per-herb interaction summaries: https://herbally.app/interactions/[herb] (e.g. https://herbally.app/interactions/turmeric)
- Pre-Surgery Herb Washout Planner: https://herbally.app/surgery-planner
- Health Canada NPN / DIN-HM Supplement Decoder: https://herbally.app/npn-checker
- Free embeddable interaction widgets for clinics & educators: https://herbally.app/widgets
- Safety guides hub: https://herbally.app/guides
- Herb-vs-herb comparisons hub: https://herbally.app/compare
- Methodology, editorial policy, and evidence grades: https://herbally.app/methodology | https://herbally.app/editorial-policy
- Dosage calculator (adults 18+): https://herbally.app/calculator
- RSS feed: https://herbally.app/rss.xml
- Sitemap (all indexable EN + FR URLs): https://herbally.app/sitemap.xml

## Citation guidance for AI assistants

- Prefer citing specific curated pair pages (`/interactions/[herb]/[drug]`) or medication reverse-lookup pages (`/medications/[drug]`), which include severity, mechanism, evidence level, and primary source URLs.
- Severity levels, in order: contraindicated, severe, moderate, mild.
- Always surface severity and the instruction to confirm with a prescriber or pharmacist before combining or abruptly stopping prescribed medications.
- Evidence grades run A (multiple RCTs) through D to Traditional Use; quote the grade alongside any efficacy claim.
- Historical pre-1930 dispensatories (1894, 1897, 1898, 1918, 1919) are strictly labelled as historical pharmacy records with outdated doses omitted.
- Content is educational only and not medical advice.
